newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - March 27.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The government has finalised the sale of a 30 percent stake in South Africa's telecommunications utility Telkom to U.S.-based SBC Communications Inc and Telekom Malaysia which will net the state $1.26 billion and lead to the delivery of 2.8 million telephone lines over five years.
- The flight of skills from government institutions had contributed to the deterioration in quality of financial management and administration, Auditor-General Henri Kluever said.

- Namakwa Sands, the mineral sands project of Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd and De Beers, will proceed with a 1.2 billion rand second phase, more than doubling annual slag output to 235,000 tonnes a year, bringing total investment in the project to 2.1 billion rand.

- Disgruntled Lonrho shareholders complained bitterly during the company's annual general meeting in London about losses and a recent warning that profit for the six months to March might fall up to a third.
- The Land Affairs department has launched the start of a huge database to identify where South Africans live, which is seen as vital to the success of the 1999 elections.
BUSINESS REPORT

- South Africa's first partial privatisation deal, the sale of a 30 percent stake in Telkom, will net 5.5 billion rand and double the number of telephone lines nationwide over a five-year period, according to communications minister Jay Naidoo.

- Preliminary findings of a special salary audit by the office of the auditor-general show that civil servants in the former black homelands may have been overpaid by more than a billion rand between 1991 and 1995.
- South African exploration company Amalia Gold has won exclusive rights to explore and develop the mineral resources of Liberia, the company said.
- Anglo American has given the green light for a 1.2 billion rand second phase of the Namakwa Sands mineral sands project to produce titanium slag, rutile, zircon and pig iron.

- New York-based merchant bank J.P. Morgan has joined the South African Futures Exchange (Safex), the first time a wholly- owned subsidiary of a U.S.-based company has become a member of the exchange.
THE STAR
- Parliamentary parties have called for immediate action to improve the government's financial management after a warning by the auditor-general of deterioration in state book-keeping.

- Sports Minister Steve Tshwete has warned South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) boss Louis Luyt that a judicial commission might be set up to probe rugby if SARFU continues to renege on an undertaking to cooperate with an investigating task group.
- South Africa's first partial privatistion deal, the sale of a 30 percent stake in Telkom, will net 5.5 billion rand and double the number of telephone lines nationwide over a five-year period.
- The first international conference to bring Zaire's warring parties together opened on Wednesday with calls for the two sides to cease fighting and start talking.
SOWETAN
- The government has spent more than 150 million rand without authority in the past financial year, the auditor-general reported.
